# Can AI write a modern jazz tune?

> An informal trial in two rounds: AI agents (Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra) each wrote a bright post-bop tune, then a dark jazz waltz, with written duo solos. Listen blind, read the sheets, and vote.

By David Reinstein (https://www.davidreinstein.org/). More projects: https://projects.davidreinstein.org/

## About

- Round 1 (26 September 2026): the same prompt went to two Claude Code sessions (Claude Opus 5.5, max effort) and one Codex session (GPT-6 Astra): an original bright post-bop tune with lydian colour and a two-chorus trumpet and guitar duo solo over its changes, with sheet music, MuseScore files and an iReal Pro chart. Tunes: Halation and Parallax (Claude), Glass Meridian (GPT-6 Astra).
- Round 2 (27-28 September 2026): a darker brief (a jazz waltz with Phrygian and sus-flat-9 sounds, a duo built on classical counterpoint, and a solo etude) given word for word to one Claude Opus 5.5 session and one GPT-6 Astra session, run unattended. Tunes: Tenebrae (Claude) and Noctilucent (GPT-6 Astra).
- The recordings are programmed sample performances of each run's own sheet music, made with one shared recipe per round, not people playing.
- The page has a blind listening section, a vote (results shown after voting), PDFs and MuseScore files for every tune, the exact prompts, and caveats. It is an informal trial, not a benchmark.
